observations.seen: Frames 1-3 read as golden hour, with a low sun down the avenue warming facades and sidewalks. Shaded areas get flat, uniform fill with no warm/cool split. In frame 4 (dusk/night) the street lamps emit no light pools and the scene goes uniformly gray.

Frame 1 shows building shadows banding the road and facades, with hard stair-step edges on the right-hand buildings. The player car has only a faint contact shadow and looks slightly floating. Poles and traffic lights cast no visible shadows.

The car's rear glass shows a single blown-out white hotspot with jagged crack-like streaks, which looks like an environment-map artifact rather than a reflection of the sun. The mint paint and the building windows show almost no environment reflection.
The city is coherent: traffic lights, lamp posts, palms, crosswalks and arrow decals. The building facades repeat the same window tiles, and frame 2's background hills are untextured orange boxes.
Frame 1's distance haze toward the sun fits the brief. In frame 2 the fog is a heavy flat orange wash that erases depth. Frame 4 has no visible fog, so the street ends in a hard skyline.

The player car's texture looks dirty and noisy. The license plate is a blurred smear, and the rear bumper shows bright streak artifacts. Buildings and road are flat diffuse colors with no roughness variation or wet/dry asphalt response.

Buildings are simple boxes and the pedestrian in frames 3-4 is a blocky primitive. The detailed yellow van in frame 2 clashes stylistically with the low-poly world and shows aliased, noisy windshield detail.

The symmetric street corridor gives a strong central vanishing point. The car's share of the frame swings from about 10% in frame 1 to about 30% in frames 3-4. The ticket card sits on top of the sun focal point in frames 1-2.
The chase camera and roughly 60-65° FOV suit the genre. In frames 3-4 the camera is pulled in tight and low, so the car blocks much of the road ahead.
The warm grade fits a film look in frames 1 and 3. Bloom is minimal even on the sun, and poles and van edges show aliasing. Frame 4 has lifted, muddy blacks and no bloom on lit windows or lamps.

The HUD in frames 1-2 is clean: timer, ticket card, score, speedometer, nitro bar and minimap. Frames 3-4 drop the timer, ticket, score, nitro bar and speed number, leaving an empty gauge. The 'Sound on (M)' text reads like debug output, and the minimap is a noisy grid of dots.
